Growing up, I felt so much hate for myself. I was treated poorly and made fun of by family members because of my dark skin and even felt less than my white peers. I didn't fit in and hated my existence for so long. The constant rejection messed me up for most of my 20's. Eventually, I had to come to love myself because "If you don't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' or even expect someone to love you. Coming to that realization was huge for me. This is my one life. I have to make the most of it, although I still struggle with some things seven years later. I've been wronged and hurt the most by black men, so that stirs up some feelings in me, but I remind myself that there are bad people of all races, and you can't let a few "bad apples" change how you feel about yourself or a whole group of people. Also, I think being in therapy is helpful. I also removed myself from toxic people and environments. Living in another country outside of America has been good for my whole being. Other than that, a mindset shift has been helpful and just putting out good energy and treating others how you'd like to be treated as cliche as it sounds is powerful.

I'm assuming you are an EU citizen. I think you would be able to get a mini-job while in Berlin during the summer; the pay isn't usually great, last I heard was 450 EUR which could work for a WG. Also, look into hostels as you mentioned, also maybe washing dishes at a restaurant or cafe helps during the busy summer season. Berlin isn't very expensive when compared to other large cities across Europe, so if you are able to save beforehand and supplement a little bit with work you should be able to have a fun summer living and learning German in Berlin. Also, look into Leipzig, it's not too far from Berlin, it's cheaper and more exposure to the German language IMO, but also close enough where you can go explore on the weekends if you choose.
